# The verifier

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_rule_docs.py from the rules and checks headgate-verify runs. Do not edit by hand. -->

`headgate-verify` reads a client package's source with ast-grep-py. It never imports the code and never touches the
network.

## Running it

```bash
uv run headgate-verify path/to/provider          # one client package
uv run headgate-verify src/                      # every client package under a directory
uv run headgate-verify --format json src/        # findings as a JSON list, for an agent or CI
```

A *client package* is a directory holding a `client.py`; every directory under the given paths that holds one is
checked, except directories named `tests` or `.venv` or starting with `.`. Each finding is one line,
`<file>:<line> <rule-id> <message>`; with `--format json` each is an object with `rule`, `path`, `line`, `message` and
`severity`.

| Exit | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | no error (warnings may have been printed) |
| `1` | at least one error |
| `2` | a usage error: no path given, a path that does not exist, or a malformed `[tool.headgate-verify]` table |

## Configuration

Two readers take `[tool.headgate-verify]` from two places. The `headgate-verify` command reads the `pyproject.toml`
nearest the **current working directory** (at or above it), not the one nearest the checked package, so run it from
the project root. The naming test's `check_names` reads the `pyproject.toml` nearest the **package's `client.py`**,
for `filler-words` and `post-reads`, unless the test passes `filler=` or `post_reads=` itself (see
[naming.md](naming.md)). Every key is a list of strings; an unknown key, or a value that is not a list of strings, is
exit `2` for the command and a `ConfigError` for `check_names`.

```toml
[tool.headgate-verify]
browser-user-agent-packages = ["scraped_portal"]   # packages whose host forces a browser User-Agent
write-name-fragments = ["order", "orders", "transfer", "withdraw", "payment"]
```

| Key | Default | Read by |
|---|---|---|
| `browser-user-agent-packages` | `[]` | `client-browser-user-agent-only-where-allowed` |
| `filler-words` | `["api", "global", "locale", "market", "markets", "us"]` | `check_names`, in the naming test |
| `post-reads` | `[]` | `check_names`, in the naming test |
| `write-name-fragments` | `["order", "orders", "payment", "transfer", "withdraw"]` | `client-order-writes-name-retry` |

`one-flavour` reads a different file: the `pyproject.toml` nearest the checked **package**, for the headgate extra
its flavour needs.

## Allow comments

A finding a reader has judged acceptable is exempted by a comment naming its rule and the reason:

```python
async def download(self, report_id: str) -> bytes:  # headgate-verify: allow client-method-shape -- a streamed body
```

The comment covers a finding on its own line, or anywhere inside the `def` or `class` whose first line carries it. A
finding against a whole module (reported at line 1) is also covered by a comment above the module's first statement,
below a licence header. An allow comment with no reason after `--`, naming an unknown rule, or suppressing nothing is
itself an error, `bad-exemption`.

## The rules

Errors fail the run; warnings never do, but the skill requires each one resolved in writing before a client is done
(an allow comment carrying the reason). The message is the rule's own; a Python check's findings each say what they
found, and the line here is the check's summary.

| Rule | Severity | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `client-accepts-transport` | error | a client's __init__ takes a `transport` parameter and passes it as HttpOptions(transport=transport) |
| `client-answer-status-is-literal` | error | a documented answer claims its status as an int literal or an HTTPStatus member |
| `client-base-url` | error | a client's base URL is a name, never a literal or an expression |
| `client-base-url-has-no-path` | error | base_url carries a path — spell the prefix out in every method's path |
| `client-browser-user-agent-only-where-allowed` | error | a browser-spoof User-Agent literal is allowed only in a package whose host forces it |
| `client-cache-with-bearer-auth` | warning | a class (of any module) that builds an `HttpCache` whose partition is not shown to be per credential, and also builds an auth that sets an `Authorization: Bearer` header, is reported once, at the first such `HttpCache(...)` call. |
| `client-constructor` | error | a client passes its rate as `rate=` in its one `super().__init__(...)`, with no splat |
| `client-default-headers-carry-no-credential` | error | credentials ride auth=, never HttpOptions(headers=) |
| `client-except-names-a-tuple-constant` | error | bind a multi-type except to a module-level tuple constant; ruff format at Python 3.14 strips the parentheses |
| `client-except-needs-review` | warning | every `except` clause of every module of the package is reported, at the clause's line, once per clause. |
| `client-impersonating-transport-owns-its-headers` | error | an AsyncCurlTransport passes default_headers=True, so curl supplies headers that match its fingerprint |
| `client-method-returns` | error | a public client method's return type says what the call returns, and never a raw Response |
| `client-method-shape` | error | a public client method is one forward of the request it was handed, or exempted with a reason |
| `client-module-has-a-client` | error | a client.py defines at least one class based directly on AsyncBaseClient |
| `client-no-hand-rolled-page-loop` | error | a page walk is `self.paginate(...)`, never a hand-written loop |
| `client-no-identity-user-agent` | error | a self-identifying User-Agent is passed in, never written as a literal |
| `client-no-placeholder-contact` | error | no placeholder contact (example.com/.org/.net) in the transport tree |
| `client-no-user-agent-beside-impersonation` | error | a module building an AsyncCurlTransport names no User-Agent where it could ride the impersonating transport |
| `client-order-writes-name-retry` | error | an order-executing or non-idempotent write names retry= (a re-sent order is a second order) |
| `client-path-constants-at-module-level` | error | a path constant is declared on the class; move it to module level |
| `client-path-holes-are-escaped-once` | error | a path hole is escaped twice; headgate escapes every t-string hole, so no quote() in one, and a verb takes the t-string itself |
| `client-paths-no-built-sink-argument` | error | a BUILT path reaches the wire; write it as a t-string (path holes are escaped by default) |
| `client-paths-no-dynamic-format-spec` | error | a format spec holds an interpolation; write the spec as a literal so `:raw` stays greppable |
| `client-paths-no-f-string` | error | an f-string carries URL structure; write the path as a t-string so headgate escapes its holes |
| `client-paths-no-format-on-path-name` | error | a path constant is rendered with .format(), which interpolates verbatim, past the verb's escaping |
| `client-paths-no-template-construction` | error | a Template is built by hand (or Template is imported under an alias); write a t-string literal instead |
| `client-pydantic-models-are-data` | error | a pydantic wire model carries fields and model_config, not methods, properties or validators |
| `client-reads-no-environment` | error | a client package reads no environment variable and loads no .env; credentials are constructor arguments |
| `client-serde-imported-by-name` | error | a seam module is bound as a module; import the names you use from headgate / headgate.msgspec / headgate.pydantic |
| `client-strings-carry-no-encoded-characters` | error | a string literal spells every character as itself; no \x, \u, \U, \N or octal escape |
| `client-transport-subclassed-not-wrapped` | error | a transport wraps another one it was handed; subclass it and call super().handle_async_request instead |
| `client-url-suffix-means-absolute` | error | a RELATIVE path is named with a _URL suffix; name it _PATH |
| `client-user-agent-has-no-default` | error | a client's user_agent has no default; the code that builds the client passes it |
| `client-wire-structs-are-data` | error | a msgspec wire struct carries fields, not computed members |
| `model-has-no-provider-prefix` | error | a model's name does not repeat the provider, which the module path already says. |
| `one-class-per-host` | error | each host the package calls has its own client class, and each class calls only its host. |
| `one-flavour` | error | a client package uses one model flavour, and its project declares that flavour's headgate extra. |
| `package-layout` | error | a client package has the files the conventions name. |

Two findings come from the verifier itself, not a rule:

| Finding | Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `bad-exemption` | error | an allow comment is malformed, has no reason, names no known rule, or drops nothing |
| `parse-error` | error | a module does not parse (Python's own parser, then tree-sitter's); no rule read it |

## What it does not check

- Method names against the docs. That is `headgate_verify.naming.check_names`, which each package's
  `test_method_names.py` runs under pytest (see [naming.md](naming.md)). The verifier checks only that the test file
  and `docs_paths.json` exist and that the snapshot follows its schema. A doc-heading method name passes the verifier
  and fails the naming test.
- Whether the client works. Its tests (see [testing.md](testing.md)) do that.
